mainTopic: Purifying תמד through השקה, then three משניות of pairs that never overlap: מכר and קנס, מיאון and חליצה, and the שופר blast and הבדלה
overview: This amud finishes a set of short rules and closes the first פרק of חולין. It opens with תמד, a weak drink made by soaking grape residue in water: before it ferments, it can be purified through השקה, touching the water of a מקוה. רבא limits this to water that was pure at first, but רב גביהה shows that the water and residue are mixed in both cases, so השקה works either way. Next come three short משניות, each with a pair of things that never happen together. The first is a father's right to sell his daughter (מכר) and the קנס fine. The second is מיאון and חליצה. For both of these pairs, רב says the משנה is only רבי מאיר's view, and חכמים let the two overlap. The third pair is the שופר blast before a holy day and הבדלה. The גמרא explains how the שופר is blown on a Friday יום טוב and where the special הבדלה wording 'בין קודש לקודש' is said. It rules against רב ששת בריה דרב אידי and against רבי דוסא, and רבי זירא explains why הבדלה lists the full set of distinctions even after a weekday יום טוב.

steps.title: Unfermented תמד can be purified by touching מקוה water
steps.stepSummary: Before תמד ferments, it can be purified through השקה. Once it has fermented, השקה no longer works.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Before it ferments] one brings it into contact with water [of a מקוה]. Once it has fermented, one does not bring it into contact with water.
steps.whatsHappening: The text picks up in the middle of a rule about תמד. Before it ferments, it can be made pure by letting it touch מקוה water. After it ferments, that method no longer works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: השקה, contact with a מקוה, can purify water. Unfermented תמד still counts as water, so השקה works on it. Once it ferments it becomes a different kind of drink, and השקה does not purify other drinks.

keyTerms.meaning: A weak drink made by soaking leftover grape residue in water
Bringing it into contact with מקוה water so that it becomes pure
It fermented or soured

phrases.english: one brings it into contact with water,
phrases.notes: "It" is the תמד, and "water" means the water of a מקוה. This applies while the תמד has not yet fermented.

phrases.english: once it has fermented, one does not bring it into contact with water.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַשִּׁיקוֹ בַּמַּיִם, מִשֶּׁהֶחְמִיץ – אֵין מַשִּׁיקוֹ בְּמַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a rule that began before this section
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Unfermented תמד can be purified through השקה. Fermented תמד cannot.

steps.title: רבא limits the rule to water that became impure later
steps.stepSummary: רבא says השקה works only if the תמד was made with pure water that later became impure, not with water that was impure from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: They taught this only when one made the תמד with pure water and it later became impure. But if the water was impure from the start, [השקה does] not [work].
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a limit to the rule we just saw. השקה only helps if the water started out pure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two cases: water that was pure when the תמד was made and became impure afterward, and water that was impure from the beginning. רבא says השקה helps only in the first case. The next step will ask what makes the two cases different.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this in the case of… (a phrase that narrows a rule)
They became impure
From the start

phrases.english: Rava said:
They taught this only where one made the temed
with pure water and it later became impure,
but if the water was impure from the start, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the rule from Step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: השקה works only for תמד made with pure water that later became impure.

steps.title: רב גביהה challenges רבא's distinction before רב אשי
steps.stepSummary: The likely reason for רבא's limit is that the heavy water sinks below the residue, so it cannot reach the מקוה. But that reason would apply equally to water that started out pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב גביהה from בי כתיל went and said this teaching before רב אשי: Why is water that was impure from the start different, so that השקה does not work? Is it because we say that since water is heavy, it settles at the bottom, the fruit residue floats on top, and the השקה does not reach the water? If so, the same should be true when the water was pure and later became impure!
steps.whatsHappening: רב גביהה questions רבא's limit. The only reason he can find for it would apply to both cases equally.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggested reason is physical: the residue floats on top and blocks the water underneath from touching the מקוה. But the layering is the same whether the water became impure early or late. So the reason cannot explain a difference between the two cases.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference?
Heavy
Floats
If so (introduces the problem with an argument)

phrases.english: Rav Geviha from Bei Katil went,
and said this teaching before Rav Ashi:
What is different about water impure from the start, that it does not work?
Because we say: since the water is heavy
it settles at the bottom,
and the fruit floats on top,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא קָא סָלְקָא לְהוּ הַשָּׁקָה לְמַיָּא.
phrases.english: and the contact does not reach the water.

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, טְהוֹרִים וּלְבַסּוֹף נִטְמְאוּ נָמֵי.
phrases.english: If so, water that was pure and later became impure should be the same too!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's distinction from Step 2
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's limit that השקה works only for water that was pure at first
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The only apparent reason, that the residue floats on top and blocks the water, would apply to both cases equally. So it cannot explain a difference between them.

steps.title: The water and residue are mixed, so השקה works in both cases
steps.stepSummary: השקה works because the water and residue are mixed together. That is true in both cases, so השקה works even when the water was impure from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, [the water and residue] are mixed together. Here too, they are mixed together.
steps.whatsHappening: רב גביהה finishes his argument against רבא. The water and residue are mixed, not layered, so השקה works in both cases and רבא's limit falls away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the residue does not block the water, the contact reaches the water in either case. The real reason השקה works applies equally to water that was impure from the start. So רבא's distinction is rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: They are mixed together
Here too

steps.whatToRemember: In the end, unfermented תמד can be purified through השקה whether its water became impure before or after it was made, because the water and residue are mixed.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not end with רבא's limit from Step 2. This step concludes that השקה works in both cases.

phrases.english: Rather, they are mixed together;
here too, they are mixed together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge from Step 3: the true reason applies to both cases, so רבא's distinction is rejected
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The water and residue are mixed, so השקה works for תמד in both cases, including water that was impure from the start.

steps.title: New משנה: sale and fine never go together
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that a father's right to sell his daughter and his right to receive the קנס never apply at the same stage of her life.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Wherever there is sale, there is no fine. And wherever there is a fine, there is no sale.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins on a new subject. It states a general rule: the father's right of sale and the fine never apply at the same time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A father may sell his daughter as an אמה עבריה only while she is a קטנה. According to this משנה, the fifty-סלע fine for rape or seduction is paid to the father only once she is a נערה. So the two belong to different stages and never overlap. The גמרא will show that חכמים disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Sale, here a father selling his young daughter as an אָמָה עִבְרִיָּה
A fixed fine, here the fifty סלעים paid to the father for rape or seduction

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule will shape the coming discussion about which ages and situations bring the fine and which bring the right of sale.

phrases.english: MISHNA:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ מֶכֶר, אֵין קְנָס,
phrases.english: Any situation where there is sale, there is no fine,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל מָקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ קְנָס, אֵין מֶכֶר.
phrases.english: and any situation where there is a fine, there is no sale.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ מֶכֶר, אֵין קְנָס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The right of sale and the קנס never apply at the same time.

steps.title: רב says the משנה follows only רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, quoting רב, says the משנה's rule that מכר and קנס never overlap is only the view of רבי מאיר. חכמים hold that קנס can apply even while she can still be sold.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: This משנה follows רבי מאיר. But חכמים said there can be a fine during the time when there is also sale.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens on the משנה from step 5 and tells us whose opinion it is. It also tells us that חכמים disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה stated a rule with no name attached. רב says it is not accepted by everyone: according to חכמים, the stage of מכר and the stage of קנס do overlap.

keyTerms.meaning: A fine the Torah requires; here, money paid to the father for violating his daughter
Sale; a father's right to sell his young daughter as a maidservant
In a place where, meaning in a situation where
The Sages, the majority opinion that argues with an individual תנא

phrases.english: GEMARA
Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
This is the view of Rabbi Meir,
but the Sages said:
there is a fine where there is sale.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells us whose opinion the משנה in step 5 follows
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה follows only רבי מאיר. חכמים hold that קנס can apply during the stage of מכר.

steps.title: The ברייתא lays out רבי מאיר's stages
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי מאיר divides a girl's life into separate stages. From birth until two hairs she can be sold but gets no קנס. From two hairs until she is fully grown she gets קנס but cannot be sold.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: a little girl from one day old until she grows two hairs can be sold but gets no fine. From two hairs until she matures, she gets a fine but cannot be sold. This is רבי מאיר's view, because he said: wherever there is sale there is no fine, and wherever there is a fine there is no sale.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove what רב just said. This first half shows that the no-overlap rule really belongs to רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Growing two hairs is the line between קטנה and נערה. For רבי מאיר, that same line turns off מכר and turns on קנס, so the two never meet.

keyTerms.meaning: A minor girl, before she shows signs of puberty
Two hairs, the sign of puberty that ends being a קטנה
Until she becomes a בוגרת, a fully grown woman
Any situation, used to introduce a general rule

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא:
A minor girl from one day old
until she grows two hairs

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁ לָהּ מֶכֶר וְאֵין לָהּ קְנָס,
phrases.english: can be sold, but has no fine.
From when she grows two hairs until she matures,

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁ לָהּ קְנָס וְאֵין לָהּ מֶכֶר,
phrases.english: she has a fine but cannot be sold.
These are the words of Rabbi Meir,
for Rabbi Meir would say:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ מֶכֶר – אֵין קְנָס,
phrases.english: Wherever there is sale, there is no fine,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל מָקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ קְנָס – אֵין מֶכֶר.
phrases.english: and wherever there is a fine, there is no sale.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source for the first half of רב's claim, that the rule belongs to רבי מאיר
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה's rule is רבי מאיר's view
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that states the same rule in רבי מאיר's name

steps.title: חכמים give קנס from age three
steps.stepSummary: The second half of the ברייתא brings חכמים, who give a girl קנס from age three and one day until she is fully grown. This covers years when she is still a קטנה and can be sold.
steps.simpleTranslation: And חכמים say: a little girl from three years and one day until she matures gets a fine.
steps.whatsHappening: This half of the ברייתא proves the second half of רב's claim, that חכמים let קנס and מכר overlap.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר starts קנס only at two hairs. חכמים start it at age three. So from age three until two hairs, she has קנס even though her father can still sell her.

keyTerms.meaning: Three years and one day, the age from which חכמים give קנס
Say, introducing the opposing opinion in a מחלוקת

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: מכר until two hairs, then קנס, never both. חכמים: קנס from age three, so it overlaps with years of מכר.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:

phrases.aramaic: קְטַנָּה מִבַּת שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד
phrases.english: A minor girl from three years and one day old
until she matures has a fine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא and shows the opinion of חכמים
steps.raayaObject: That חכמים allow קנס during the years of מכר
steps.raayaSupportSource: The opinion of חכמים in the same ברייתא

steps.title: Do חכמים mean she cannot be sold?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about the wording of חכמים. They mention only קנס. Does that mean she has קנס but not מכר? That cannot be right, since a father can sell his young daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: A fine, yes, but sale, no?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of חכמים in the ברייתא. It sounds as if they took away the father's right to sell her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חכמים said "she has a fine" and said nothing about מכר. Read on its own, that sounds like a swap: קנס instead of מכר. But a father's right to sell his קטנה is not in question, so the wording is hard to accept.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes
No

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying חכמים really take away מכר. It only asks why their wording sounds that way.

phrases.english: A fine, yes,
but sale, no?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of חכמים in step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording of חכמים in the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Mentioning only קנס suggests there is no מכר, but a father can surely sell his young daughter.

steps.title: Read it as קנס even during מכר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that חכמים mean she has קנס as well, even while she can still be sold. They are adding קנס, not removing מכר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: there is also a fine where there is sale.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by explaining what חכמים really meant. This matches רב's quote from step 6.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אף ("also") changes the meaning. חכמים are not trading מכר for קנס. They are saying both rights exist together during those years, which is exactly what רב said.

keyTerms.meaning: Say, meaning read the statement this way
Also, even

steps.whatToRemember: For חכמים, from age three until two hairs, the father can both sell his daughter and collect קנס. Only רבי מאיר keeps the two apart.

phrases.english: Say: there is also a fine where there is sale.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9
steps.terutzHavaAmina: חכמים meant she has קנס instead of מכר.
steps.terutzMaskana: חכמים meant she has קנס in addition to מכר.

steps.title: New משנה: מיאון and חליצה never apply together
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה gives another pair that never overlaps. When a girl can do מיאון, she cannot do חליצה. When she can do חליצה, she can no longer do מיאון.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Wherever there is refusal, there is no חליצה. Wherever there is חליצה, there is no refusal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new משנה. It follows the same pattern as the last one: two rules that apply at different stages of life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מיאון applies only to a קטנה married off by her mother or brothers. חליצה applies only once she is grown. So the stage that allows one rule shuts out the other.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; marks the start of a new משנה
Refusal; a young girl married off by her mother or brothers can walk out of the marriage
The ceremony that frees a childless widow from marrying her husband's brother

phrases.english: MISHNA

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ מֵיאוּן – אֵין חֲלִיצָה,
phrases.english: Wherever there is refusal, there is no חליצה,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל מָקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ חֲלִיצָה – אֵין מֵיאוּן.
phrases.english: and wherever there is חליצה, there is no refusal.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ מֵיאוּן – אֵין חֲלִיצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה with the same pattern of two rules that never meet
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מיאון and חליצה never apply at the same stage: מיאון belongs to a קטנה, and חליצה belongs to a grown woman.

steps.title: רב says the rule about refusal and release follows only רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: רב, quoted by רב יהודה, says the משנה's rule (no מיאון where there is חליצה) is only the view of רבי מאיר. חכמים hold that מיאון and חליצה can overlap.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: This rule is the view of רבי מאיר. But חכמים say a girl can do מיאון even at a stage when she could also do חליצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts on the משנה from step 11 and tells us whose opinion it is. רב says it is only רבי מאיר, and חכמים disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that מיאון and חליצה never happen at the same stage of a girl's life. רב says this is not everyone's view. According to חכמים there is a stretch of time when she can do both.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
Refusal: a young girl married off by her mother or brothers can cancel the marriage by refusing
The ceremony that releases a widow from marrying her late husband's brother
The Sages, the group that argues with a single named תנא
In a situation where, at the same time as

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
This is the view of Rabbi Meir,
phrases.notes: "This" is the rule in the משנה from step 11: when she can do מיאון she cannot do חליצה.

phrases.english: but the Sages say:
there is refusal in a situation where there is ḥalitza,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה, אָמַר רַב: זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells us whose opinion the משנה of step 11 follows and shows that חכמים disagree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rule that מיאון and חליצה never overlap belongs to רבי מאיר. חכמים allow מיאון even when she can already do חליצה.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows the two opinions on how long a girl may refuse
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא proves רב's claim. רבי מאיר says מיאון lasts only until two hairs appear. רבי יהודה says it lasts until the black hair covers more than the white skin, which is later.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a ברייתא: Until when can a girl do מיאון? Until she grows two hairs. That is רבי מאיר's view. רבי יהודה says: until the black hair covers more area than the white skin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up רב. It shows that רבי יהודה (the חכמים of step 12) lets מיאון go on longer than רבי מאיר does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, מיאון ends at two hairs, the same moment she becomes an adult who can do חליצה, so the two never overlap. For רבי יהודה, מיאון goes on past two hairs, into the time when she can already do חליצה. That shared stretch is what חכמים meant by "יש מיאון במקום חליצה."

keyTerms.meaning: Refuses; does מיאון
Two hairs: the sign that a girl has become an adult
Until the black (hair) covers more than the white (skin): a later stage of growing up

steps.confusionAlert: Step 12 said "חכמים," but the ברייתא names רבי יהודה. Here the חכמים of רב's statement are רבי יהודה.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: מיאון ends exactly when חליצה becomes possible, so they never overlap. רבי יהודה: מיאון goes on a bit longer, so there is a time when both are possible.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:
Until when may a girl refuse?
Until she grows two hairs,
the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
Until the black is greater than the white.
phrases.notes: He means the black hair covers more area than the bare white skin. By then she can already do חליצה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רב's claim in step 12.
steps.raayaObject: That חכמים (רבי יהודה) allow מיאון at a stage when חליצה is already possible
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where רבי מאיר ends מיאון at two hairs and רבי יהודה ends it when the black is greater than the white

steps.title: New משנה: שופר blasts and הבדלה never happen together
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה gives another pair that never overlaps. Wherever there is תקיעה there is no הבדלה, and wherever there is הבדלה there is no תקיעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Any time there is a שופר blast, there is no הבדלה. Any time there is הבדלה, there is no שופר blast.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens with a new pair of things that never come together: תקיעה and הבדלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This keeps the משנה's pattern of "wherever X, not Y." The תקיעה here is the shofar blown before a holy day starts, to tell people to stop working. הבדלה is said when a holy day ends.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
A shofar blast, here the one blown before a holy day to mark its start
The blessing that separates a holy day from the day after it

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Any situation where there is a shofar blast,
phrases.notes: This is the shofar blown on Friday afternoon (or before יום טוב) to tell people to stop working.

phrases.english: there is no havdala,
and any situation where there is havdala,
there is no shofar blast.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ תְּקִיעָה – אֵין הַבְדָּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of pairs that never overlap, now with a new pair.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תקיעה and הבדלה never happen together.

steps.title: The two cases: יום טוב on Friday or right after שבת
steps.stepSummary: If יום טוב falls on Friday, we blow the שופר but do not say הבדלה. If יום טוב falls right after שבת, we say הבדלה but do not blow.
steps.simpleTranslation: If יום טוב falls on ערב שבת, we blow the שופר and do not say הבדלה. If it falls on מוצאי שבת, we say הבדלה and do not blow.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה shows its rule from step 14 with two cases where a יום טוב sits next to שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Going from יום טוב into שבת, we move into the holier day, so we blow to tell people to stop the work that was allowed on יום טוב, and we do not say הבדלה. Going from שבת into יום טוב, we move down to the less holy day, so we say הבדלה, and there is nothing new to stop, so we do not blow.

keyTerms.meaning: A Festival day
That happens to fall on
Friday, the day before שבת
The night after שבת ends

phrases.aramaic: יוֹם טוֹב שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת –
phrases.english: A Festival that falls on Shabbat eve:
we sound the shofar, and we do not recite havdala;
at the conclusion of Shabbat:
phrases.notes: The words "a Festival that falls" are understood here too, just like in the first case.

phrases.english: we recite havdala, and we do not sound the shofar.

steps.triggerLanguage: יוֹם טוֹב שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת – תּוֹקְעִין, וְלֹא מַבְדִּילִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the rule of step 14 with real cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יום טוב on Friday: blow, no הבדלה. יום טוב on מוצאי שבת: הבדלה, no blowing.

steps.title: The wording of הבדלה when שבת leads into יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks how we say הבדלה from שבת into יום טוב. The answer is with the ending "המבדיל בין קודש לקודש."
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we say הבדלה? We say: "Who separates between holy and holy."
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה goes back to the second case from step 15 and tells us the wording of that special הבדלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A normal מוצאי שבת הבדלה separates holy from weekday (קודש לחול). Here both days are holy, so the ending changes to "between holy and holy."

keyTerms.meaning: How?
Who separates: the ending words of the הבדלה blessing
Holy, here a holy day

phrases.english: How does one recite havdala?
phrases.notes: He means the הבדלה said when שבת ends and יום טוב begins.

phrases.english: "Who separates between holy and holy."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how to carry out the הבדלה from step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הבדלה from שבת into יום טוב ends "בין קודש לקודש."

steps.title: רבי דוסא's wording: greater holiness and lesser holiness
steps.stepSummary: רבי דוסא says the ending should be "between greater holiness and lesser holiness."
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי דוסא says: "Between stricter holiness and lighter holiness."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי דוסא gives a different wording for the same הבדלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions agree that both days are holy. רבי דוסא wants the blessing to also say that שבת is holier than יום טוב, so it names one as "חמור" and the other as "קל."

keyTerms.meaning: Stricter, greater holiness: שבת
Lighter, lesser holiness: יום טוב
Strict and lenient: more and less serious

steps.whatToRemember: תקיעה marks moving up into a holier day, and הבדלה marks moving down from a holier day, so they never meet. Between שבת and יום טוב, the הבדלה wording speaks of two kinds of holiness.

phrases.english: Rabbi Dosa says:
"Between greater holiness and lesser holiness."
phrases.notes: The "greater holiness" is שבת and the "lesser holiness" is יום טוב.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי דּוֹסָא אוֹמֵר: בֵּין קוֹדֶשׁ חָמוּר לְקוֹדֶשׁ הַקַּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the wording given in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי דוסא: the הבדלה ends "בין קודש חמור לקודש הקל."

steps.title: How is the שופר blown on a Friday יום טוב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking how exactly one blows the שופר when יום טוב falls on Friday.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: How does one blow?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts by asking a practical question about the משנה's case of blowing on a Friday יום טוב. This sets up the answers of רב יהודה and רב אסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said we blow on a Friday יום טוב but did not say how. On a regular Friday the blowing to announce שבת has a set pattern. The גמרא wants to know what changes when the day is already יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion of the אמוראים on the משנה
How? In what way?
Blows the שופר (a long blast)

phrases.english: GEMARA:
How does one blow?
phrases.notes: This goes back to the משנה's case of יום טוב on Friday, when we blow but do not say הבדלה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the משנה to the גמרא's discussion of the blowing case
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact way the שופר is blown on a יום טוב that falls on Friday

steps.title: רב יהודה: the תרועה comes out of the תקיעה
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says one blows a תקיעה and lets the תרועה come out of the middle of that same blast.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: He blows a long blast and makes the broken sounds from inside the long blast.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה gives the first answer. The broken sounds (תרועה) are made without stopping the long blast (תקיעה).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a תקיעה and a תרועה are separate sounds. רב יהודה says that on a Friday יום טוב they are joined, with the תרועה growing out of the middle of the תקיעה. This changes the usual pattern a little because the day is already holy.

keyTerms.meaning: A long, steady שופר blast
Blows a תְּרוּעָה, a series of short broken blasts
From inside the long blast, without a break

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
He blows a long blast and makes the broken sounds from inside the long blast,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: תּוֹקֵעַ וּמֵרִיעַ מִתּוֹךְ תְּקִיעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תרועה is made from inside the תקיעה, as one continuous sound

steps.title: רב אסי: תקיעה and תרועה in one breath
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי says the תקיעה and the תרועה are blown in one breath, and he set this up as the practice in הוצל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב אסי said: He blows a long blast and then the broken sounds, all in one breath. רב אסי set up this practice in הוצל, following his own ruling.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי gives a different answer: the two sounds are separate but done in a single breath. The גמרא adds that he actually made this the practice in the town of הוצל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב אסי, the long blast stops and then the broken sounds come, but the blower does not take a new breath in between. That is different from רב יהודה, where the sound never stops at all. The story of הוצל shows this was a real practice, not just a theory.

keyTerms.meaning: One breath
He set up (an official practice)
According to his own ruling

phrases.english: And Rav Asi said:
He blows a long blast and the broken sounds in one breath.
Rav Asi set up the practice in Huzal
phrases.notes: הוצל is the name of a town in בבל.

phrases.english: according to his ruling.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב אַסִּי אָמַר: תּוֹקֵעַ וּמֵרִיעַ בִּנְשִׁימָה אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer that argues with רב יהודה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תקיעה and the תרועה are separate sounds, but they are blown in one breath

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to say there is no תרועה at all
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that on a Friday יום טוב we blow a תקיעה but not a תרועה, which seems to argue with both אמוראים.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: On a יום טוב that falls on Friday, we blow long blasts and do not blow broken sounds. Doesn't this mean no broken sounds at all?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to say the תרועה is skipped completely. That would argue with both רב יהודה and רב אסי, since both of them include a תרועה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both אמוראים agree that some kind of תרועה is blown; they only argue about how. The ברייתא's words 'ולא מריעין' sound like no תרועה at all. If that reading is right, both opinions are in trouble.

keyTerms.meaning: Friday, the day before שבת
Doesn't it mean...? (a pushing question)
At all

phrases.english: They challenged:

phrases.aramaic: יוֹם טוֹב שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת,
phrases.english: A יום טוב that falls on Friday,
we blow long blasts and do not blow broken sounds.
Doesn't it mean no broken sounds at all?

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: יוֹם טוֹב שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks both answers from steps 19 and 20
steps.kashyaTarget: Both רב יהודה and רב אסי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both opinions include a תרועה, but the ברייתא seems to say no תרועה is blown at all

steps.title: רב יהודה reads the ברייתא his own way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that each אמורא reads the ברייתא to fit his view. For רב יהודה, it means no separate תרועה, only one from inside the תקיעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. רב יהודה explains it his way, and רב אסי explains it his way. רב יהודה explains it his way: we do not blow broken sounds on their own, only from inside the long blast.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the reading that there is no תרועה at all. It says each sage explains the ברייתא to match his opinion, starting with רב יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ולא מריעין' does not mean 'no תרועה ever.' For רב יהודה it means no תרועה as a separate sound. The תרועה is still there, but it comes out of the תקיעה.

keyTerms.meaning: Explains the source according to his own reasoning
On its own, as a separate thing

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not being thrown out. Both sages accept it; they only explain what 'no תרועה' really means.

phrases.english: No,
Rav Yehuda explains it according to his reasoning
and Rav Asi explains it according to his reasoning.
Rav Yehuda explains it according to his reasoning:
we do not blow broken sounds on their own,
but only from inside the long blast.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, רַב יְהוּדָה מְתָרֵץ לְטַעְמֵיהּ וְרַב אַסִּי מְתָרֵץ לְטַעְמֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21 for רב יהודה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'ולא מריעין' means no תרועה at all
steps.terutzMaskana: For רב יהודה it means no separate תרועה; the תרועה comes from inside the תקיעה

steps.title: רב אסי reads the ברייתא his own way
steps.stepSummary: For רב אסי, the ברייתא means the תרועה is not blown with a second breath, only in the same breath as the תקיעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב אסי explains it his way: we do not blow the broken sounds in two breaths, but in one breath.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives רב אסי's reading of the same ברייתא. This finishes the answer to the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב אסי, 'ולא מריעין' means no תרועה with a fresh breath. The תרועה is still blown, but in the same breath as the תקיעה. So the ברייתא fits both opinions, and neither one is pushed off.

keyTerms.meaning: Two breaths

steps.whatToRemember: On a Friday יום טוב, both sages hold a תרועה is blown. רב יהודה: it comes out of the middle of the תקיעה. רב אסי: it comes right after, in the same breath. The ברייתא's 'no תרועה' fits each view.

phrases.english: And Rav Asi explains it according to his reasoning:
we do not blow the broken sounds in two breaths,
but in one breath.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer of step 22, now for רב אסי
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'ולא מריעין' means no תרועה at all
steps.terutzMaskana: For רב אסי it means no תרועה with a second breath; it is blown in one breath with the תקיעה

steps.title: Where in הבדלה is the special ending said?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about יום טוב after שבת and asks where in the blessing the wording 'between holy and holy' is said.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And after שבת, etc.' Where does he say it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second case of the משנה, הבדלה when יום טוב comes right after שבת. It asks where in the blessing the special wording goes, which sets up the next answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה taught the wording 'המבדיל בין קודש לקודש.' The הבדלה blessing has an opening part and a closing line. The גמרא asks whether the special wording replaces the usual words in the opening, the closing, or both.

keyTerms.meaning: The night right after שבת ends
Where?
Etc., the rest of the quote

phrases.english: 'And after שבת, etc.'
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה from steps 15 and 16 about יום טוב that comes right after שבת.

phrases.english: Where does he say it?
phrases.notes: 'It' means the special wording 'between holy and holy.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְמוֹצָאֵי שַׁבָּת כּוּ׳. הֵיכָא אָמַר לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the שופר topic and opens the הבדלה topic
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In which part of the הבדלה blessing the wording 'בין קודש לקודש' is said

steps.title: רב יהודה and רב נחמן: only at the closing line
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה and רב נחמן both say the special wording is said in the closing line of the blessing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: In its closing line. And רב נחמן also said: In its closing line.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give the same answer: the special wording goes in the ending of the blessing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The body of the blessing keeps its usual wording, like any מוצאי שבת. Only the closing line changes to 'המבדיל בין קודש לקודש.' רב נחמן's agreement makes this view stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: The closing line of a blessing (the part starting 'ברוך אתה')
And likewise; another sage says the same

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
In its closing line,
and likewise Rav Nachman said:
In its closing line.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The special wording is said only in the closing line

steps.title: רב ששת בריה דרב אידי: also at the opening
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת בריה דרב אידי says the special wording is said at the beginning of the blessing too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב ששת son of רב אידי said: Even at its opening.
steps.whatsHappening: A third אמורא disagrees. He says the special wording is also used in the opening part of the blessing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For him, the usual opening words 'between holy and ordinary' are swapped for 'between holy and holy' as well. So the change shows up twice, at the start and at the end.

keyTerms.meaning: The opening part of a blessing
Even, also

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי אָמַר:
phrases.english: And Rav Sheshet son of Rav Idi said:
Even at its opening,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי אָמַר: אַף בִּפְתִיחָתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues with step 25
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The special wording is said at the opening as well as the closing

steps.title: The הלכה does not follow רב ששת בריה דרב אידי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that the הלכה does not follow רב ששת בריה דרב אידי, so the special wording goes only in the closing line.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is not like him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling on the הבדלה question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the הלכה does not follow רב ששת בריה דרב אידי, we follow רב יהודה and רב נחמן. The opening keeps its regular wording, and only the closing line says 'בין קודש לקודש.'

keyTerms.meaning: And the הלכה is not like him

steps.whatToRemember: When יום טוב comes right after שבת, the הבדלה opening stays as usual, and only the closing line says 'המבדיל בין קודש לקודש.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical wording of הבדלה (said in קידוש) on a יום טוב night that comes right after שבת.

phrases.english: And the הלכה is not like him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between steps 25 and 26
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The special הבדלה wording is said only in the closing line, as רב יהודה and רב נחמן said

steps.title: רבי דוסא's wording: greater holiness and lesser holiness
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רבי דוסא's opinion from the משנה: when יום טוב follows שבת, one says 'between greater holiness and lesser holiness'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי דוסא says: one says 'between greater holiness and lesser holiness'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי דוסא from the משנה. He holds that when יום טוב starts right after שבת, the הבדלה should say 'between greater holiness and lesser holiness'. The גמרא is quoting him so it can rule on his view in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא of the משנה just says 'between holy and holy'. רבי דוסא adds detail: שבת is the greater holiness and יום טוב is the lesser one. So his version spells out which way the step down goes.

keyTerms.meaning: Greater (more serious) holiness, meaning שבת here
Lesser (lighter) holiness, meaning יום טוב here

phrases.english: Rabbi Dosa says:
'Between greater holiness and lesser holiness,'
phrases.notes: The greater holiness is שבת, which is ending. The lesser holiness is יום טוב, which is starting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling where 'between holy and holy' is said, the גמרא turns to the other opinion in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי דוסא, the הבדלה wording is 'between greater holiness and lesser holiness'.

steps.title: The הלכה does not follow רבי דוסא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that the הלכה is not like רבי דוסא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is not like him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a ruling: we do not use רבי דוסא's longer wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the הלכה is not like רבי דוסא, the practical wording stays the simple 'between holy and holy' of the תנא קמא. Together with step 27, this fixes both the words and where they are said.

keyTerms.meaning: The הלכה is not like him

steps.whatToRemember: When יום טוב follows שבת, the closing line of הבדלה says 'between holy and holy'. It does not say 'greater holiness and lesser holiness'.

phrases.english: And the halakha is not in accordance with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules against the opinion quoted in step 28.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: We use the תנא קמא's wording 'between holy and holy', not רבי דוסא's.

steps.title: רבי זירא: the full list of distinctions even after a weekday יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא teaches that at the end of a יום טוב that falls during the week, one says the full הבדלה, including 'between the seventh day and the six working days'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: when יום טוב falls in the middle of the week, one says: 'Who distinguishes between holy and ordinary, between light and darkness, between Israel and the nations, and between the seventh day and the six working days.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא gives a new rule about the הבדלה said when a weekday יום טוב ends. One says the regular full list, the same one used after שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sounds strange, because the day that is ending is not the seventh day, so why mention it? Even so, רבי זירא keeps that line in. This sets up the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: In the middle of the week (here שַׁבָּת means 'week')
'Who distinguishes', the key words of the הבדלה blessing
Holy and ordinary (weekday)
The six working days

steps.confusionAlert: 'בְּאֶמְצַע שַׁבָּת' does not mean 'in the middle of שבת'. Here שַׁבָּת means 'the week', so it is a יום טוב on a weekday.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:

phrases.aramaic: יוֹם טוֹב שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּאֶמְצַע שַׁבָּת,
phrases.english: A Festival that falls in the middle of the week,
one says: 'Who distinguishes between holy and ordinary,
and between light and darkness,
and between Israel and the nations,

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵין יוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי לְשֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה״,
phrases.english: and between the seventh day and the six days of work,'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from יום טוב after שבת to a related case: the end of a weekday יום טוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After a weekday יום טוב, one says the full הבדלה, including 'between the seventh day and the six working days'.

steps.title: Why mention the seventh day?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבי זירא's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why one would mention the seventh day when the day ending is not שבת. It is setting up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a request for the reason, not an attack. The puzzle is that the line about the seventh day does not seem to fit a weekday יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind step 30.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the line 'between the seventh day and the six working days' is said after a יום טוב that is not שבת.

steps.title: He is listing the set of distinctions
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the blessing is a fixed list of the distinctions, not a description of this particular day.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is listing the series of distinctions.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that הבדלה simply lists the set of distinctions חז״ל put into the blessing. So the seventh-day line stays in even when it does not describe today.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blessing is not meant to describe exactly what is ending tonight. It praises the general idea of הבדלה by listing the standard distinctions in order, so every line is said each time.

keyTerms.meaning: The set order of distinctions
Lists, counts

steps.whatToRemember: The הבדלה blessing is a fixed list of distinctions. That is why after a weekday יום טוב we still say 'between the seventh day and the six working days'.

phrases.english: He is enumerating the series of distinctions.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 31.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The blessing lists the standard set of distinctions, so the seventh-day line is said even when it does not describe the day that is ending.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק הכל שוחטין
steps.stepSummary: The closing words of the first פרק of חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, 'הכל שוחטין'.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the הדרן, the traditional line said when finishing a פרק. It closes the first פרק of מסכת חולין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is not part of the argument. It marks the end of the פרק and expresses our wish to come back and learn it again.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (said at the end of a פרק)
'Everyone may slaughter', the name of the first פרק of חולין

phrases.english: We will return to you, 'Everyone may slaughter.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק after the final teaching about הבדלה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The first פרק of מסכת חולין, הכל שוחטין, is complete.
